name: Koko Dhawa
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Black, Paul. 1980. Norman Pama historical phonology. Papers in Australian Linguistics 13, 181-239 (PL A-59); Black 2010 (Co-narration of a Koko-Bera story, PL 626); Black & Koch 1983 (Aboriginal History 7); Busby 1979 (ANU MA); Carrington & Triffitt 1999 OZBIB (PL D-92)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent Thawa/Dhawa/Kok-Thaw: no mention of Koko Dhawa in any of them; OZBIB 1999 has no entry for Sommer 1997 or Ethnografix. (For the sister language Koko-Bera, Black 1980 p.198 says stress is contrastive; that is not a statement about Koko Dhawa.)

sources.citation: AUSTLANG Y93 Kok Thawa language record (AIATSIS)
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy. the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.note: Would list AIATSIS holdings and documentation for Y93 (manuscripts, wordlists, recordings), including whether Sommer 1997 or Sommer field notes are held at AIATSIS.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and GitHub md.ini for koko1272 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Lists a single reference (Sommer 1997), alt names Bidhidj / Uw Inal, status extinct, sister of Gugubera/Kok Kaper [kkp] in 'Dhawa-Kaber'. Note: Glottolog 5.1 extract) lists 0 descriptive refs; the 5.3 page and hh.bib do carry Sommer 1997 as a grammar sketch.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Gugu Dhaw language' (en) and 'Idioma kok thawa' (es); Wikidata Q5615279
sources.note: Stubs: names, classification, AIATSIS Y93, Glottolog koko1272; references only AUSTLANG Y93 and Dixon 2002 (Australian Languages, p. xxxii, a list). No phonology or stress content.

sources.citation: Sommer, Bruce A. 1997. Koko Dhawa. Townsville: Ethnografix. 19 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only descriptive work on the language that Glottolog knows (listed by Glottolog as a grammar sketch); a 19-page sketch will almost certainly contain a phonology/orthography section with a stress remark, as Sommer's other sketches do. Held as a non-shareable scan by Glottolog (nosharefn). Not found in JCU or UQ catalogues; check AIATSIS Library (Mura) and NLA/Trove, or ask Harald Hammarström / Bruce Sommer.

sources.note: Sketch of the sister language Koko-Bera by the same author, from the same fieldwork; may discuss Koko Dhawa as a neighbouring variety and its stress; also unshared.
